executiveSummary: GM0246 passes the complete deterministic execution contract for all ten canonical presets, T+0/6/12/24/48/72 and all eight essential services. Its 2025 CBS/PDOK identity, 19,305 residents, fifteen neighbourhoods, four BAG places, thirteen BRT settlement labels, 22 scheduled-transit stop areas and three A50/N794 municipal-border links are coherent. Current NWB semantics correctly limit roads to Mobility and assumed road-logistics Supply. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Heerde has a genuine, operationally specific IJssel pathway: the eight-kilometre Veessen–Wapenveld high-water channel is activated above 5.65 m NAP at Veessen, temporarily makes the area between channel and IJssel an island, changes the state of inlet/outlet works and Gemaal Doornbos and is expected to remain active for about 1.5 months. LIWO also exposes two primary candidate breach locations inside GM0246. The model selects none of these states while assigning 2.708946 normalized river inundation stress from T+12 through T+72, 9,224 affected people-equivalent at T+24 and 9,805 at T+72. Eight unrelated nonzero hazard families reuse one exact neighbourhood order, and a controlled ignition inside both official Heerde186 mixed-forest eligibility and current TOP10NL conifer forest leaves its source neighbourhood sixth. The graph omits Kerkdijk over the inlet, the east-side village access/islanding problem, Wapenveld drainage, external acute-care routes and the water-control sequence. Public registers, policies, observations and official scenarios can improve fidelity, but they remain distinct from event state. NoData, no selected event and a filtered no-match never mean zero, open or safe.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Omgevingsvisie Heerde, adopted 27 May 2024
supports: The municipality distinguishes the Veluwe, IJssel uiterwaarden/high-water channel, wet Weteringengebied and village areas. It names IJssel, high-water channel, Apeldoorns Kanaal, streams, springs, ditches and weteringen as different water systems.

Kerkdijk is the principal connection between Veessen/Vorchten and Heerde and crosses the high-water-channel inlet. The wet Weteringengebied drains north toward a pump at Wapenveld and has IJssel seepage risk.

The Veluwe portion is crossed by A50 and local roads and contains forests/heath, Renderklippen and busy Heerderstrand recreation. Municipal climate adaptation addresses cloudbursts, drought, heat and nature fire as distinct risks.
The adopted vision is policy/planning evidence with no live event API, fixed machine cadence or standard reuse licence stated. It does not prove current route, visitor, water, fire or response state.

evidenceSources.publisher: Waterschap Vallei en Veluwe and Rijkswaterstaat
evidenceSources.title: E03 — Hoogwatergeul Veessen–Wapenveld operating and drainage context
evidenceSources.edition: High-water channel constructed 2012–2017; current operator page retrieved 2026-09-03
supports: The eight-kilometre, 550–1,500 m wide channel is activated when the IJssel reaches 5.65 m+NAP at Veessen; sixty 12 m × 1.05 m inlet flaps are opened in stages and about 40% of IJssel flow can use the channel.

Activation can lower IJssel level by roughly 71 cm at Veessen, temporarily makes the land between channel and IJssel an island and is expected to last about 1.5 months. These are design/operating semantics, not a current activation.

Gemaal Doornbos normally uses three pumps with joint capacity 175 m³/min; it is switched off while the channel is active, then free drainage, an outlet sluice and later Doornbos restore levels according to stated thresholds.

The operator page provides thresholds and sequence but not live flap/pump state, telemetry licence, current capacity, failure, forecast hydrograph or guaranteed restoration. Rijkswaterstaat separately describes the channel as a Ruimte voor de Rivier bypass.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — LIWO 2025.1.6 primary breach catalogue and flood-scenario contract

No regional, regional-water-system or outside-dike candidate point is returned in the same envelope. No-record is a scoped catalogue result, not proof that those mechanisms are impossible or safe.
A candidate point and frequency flags do not select a breach, defence/control state, hydrograph, probability, connected footprint or consequence grid.

IPLO requires specialist water-management expertise. Causal use must pin release, scenario/model dates, source water, breach/overtopping/control variant, native CRS/resolution/units/NoData, depth, velocity, arrival, duration, recession and scenario-clock mapping. Exact redistribution terms for persisted LIWO products require confirmation.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Regionaal Risicoprofiel and Dekkingsplan 2025–2028

The region is approximately 25% forest/heath and receives about 1.4 million recreational visitors at regional scale. Nature-fire consequences depend on ignition, wind, terrain, fuel, vulnerable objects, evacuation and scarce specialist capacity.
Flood planning requires named source/defence, lead time, footprint, warning/evacuation decision and cross-agency coordination; a generic centroid-distance field does not supply these.

This is strategic four-year planning evidence with no live machine event feed or standard data-reuse licence stated. It does not establish current probability, resources, coverage, utility state or checkpoint completion.

residualLimitations: This audits a deterministic first-72-hour exercise model, not a forecast, warning, flood assessment, evacuation plan, wildfire prediction, public-health instruction or operator commitment.
CBS values are rounded/suppressed and neighbourhood totals need not equal the municipality total; null heating/charging and absent operational records remain Unknown.
The overview boundary is selection/aggregation geometry only; full-resolution and native infrastructure/hazard geometry is required for channel, flood, fire, road and asset intersection.
LIWO candidates and scenario rasters are modeled planning evidence requiring expert selection and complete release/model/spatial/NoData provenance; candidate presence is not breach or probability.
Published Veessen–Wapenveld thresholds, dimensions and Doornbos capacity are design/operation context, not current flap/pump state, structural condition, command or guaranteed performance.
HWH/DAMO objects do not establish connected catchments, compatible throughput, live controls, power/backup, water quality, overflow or restoration.
Risicokaart/TOP10NL forest identifies old/current eligibility context, not ignition, fuel/moisture, perimeter, smoke, visitors, access, firewater or suppression.
NWB/NDW/GTFS and municipal plans do not establish incident-time route passability, transport vehicles, emergency exemptions, evacuation capacity or hospital reachability.
Waterinfo's 16 cm observation is a point/time value outside the synthetic scenario clock; it does not calibrate the river run or prove later safety.

No complete public physical electricity, gas, drinking-water, wastewater, telecom, facility, fuel, stock, staff, backup, repair or restoration topology is consumed; sensitive gaps remain Unknown or synthetic.
Resident allocation omits Veluwe/Heerderstrand visitors, workers, patients, responders and actual people east of the channel at activation time.
Earthquake, cyber, weather and remote-smoke presets remain generic exercises unless a named event/target and valid-time forcing are selected.
A 1.5-month channel design-duration context extends beyond T+72; long-duration flooding, recovery and cross-boundary effects into Hattem/Epe/Olst-Wijhe/Isala remain outside validated scope.
